cases.claim: Precision is the accuracy of a measurement or prediction, and can be calculated by subtracting the lowest measured value from the highest measured value.

reference_parts.text: Measurement precision is the same as measurement accuracy.
reference_parts.label: contradicted
reference_parts.evidence_quote: Precision is not the same as accuracy. Accuracy measures how close experimental values come to the true or theoretical value, while precision measures how close the measured values are to each other.
reference_parts.reason: The source explicitly distinguishes the concepts. This is an additional relation category, not relabeled as a number error.

reference_parts.text: A precision measure can be calculated by subtracting the lowest measured value from the highest.
reference_parts.label: supported
reference_parts.evidence_quote: The range of a set of data is the difference between the highest and lowest measurements. Just subtract one from the other.
reference_parts.reason: The article permits reporting range as a precision measure; it does not call range the only precision measure.

cases.human_review_note: User confirmed both proposed labels after seeing the saved-source distinction between precision and accuracy and its allowance of range as a precision measure. AI-assisted review; not independent annotation.
